answer.label: Francis — modern English translation
answer.sourceLine: The Cord prints the exact sentence and identifies Admonition XIX.2, citing Francis of Assisi: Early Documents, volume 1, page 135. Daniel Horan’s article supplies the 1999 New City Press edition reference. That modern translation was not independently opened as a book; the checked 1906 Robinson translation has different wording and numbering.

author.name: Francis of Assisi
author.heading: About Francis of Assisi
author.bio: Francis of Assisi founded the religious movement that became the Franciscan order. His surviving rules, letters and admonitions address life together, humility and service. English quotations from those writings depend on the particular translator; the medieval author did not write these English sentences.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: In Robinson’s 1906 English translation, Admonition 20 contrasts a servant’s conduct when praised with conduct when dismissed or looked down upon. Its point is humility before God rather than dependence on public esteem. That related passage differs in wording and numbering from the modern Early Documents translation quoted above. Robinson’s 1906 translation ↗
